Workshop setup guide — AI-assisted Astro website building

Welcome! By the end of this workshop, you'll have a fast, SEO-strong website built with an AI coding assistant as your pair programmer. No professional coding experience is required. This guide takes you from zero to ready to build.

Total setup time: allow about 60–75 minutes, including downloads and a full project check. Complete it at least one day before the workshop if you can. If you hit a snag, send Big Chris the step number and the exact error message.

Don't stress if setup takes longer than expected. Developer tooling can be fiddly even for experienced engineers. The workshop is designed so people can catch up during exercises, and Big Chris will help troubleshoot.

The important finish line: do not stop after installing the tools. In Step 11 you will install the workshop project's dependencies, build the site, and open it in your browser. That final check is what proves you are ready.

Start here: follow the numbered steps in order

Begin with Step 1 and complete each “You're done” check before moving to the next step. Even if you already have some tools installed, verify them when their step appears. Do not open several installer links and work through them in a different order.

Every download link appears in the step where it is needed. A reference list is at the very end of this guide, after the checklist.

About your choice of AI assistant

This workshop is AI-tool agnostic. Choose Claude Code or Codex inside VS Code, or use Antigravity IDE with its built-in assistant.

Antigravity users: wherever later steps say “VS Code”, use Antigravity IDE instead. Open the project, terminal, and assistant in that same editor.

Your assistant needs to be able to:

  • read and edit files in the project you have open in your editor;
  • run terminal commands after asking your permission; and
  • read the workshop's project-instructions file when you ask it to.

Steps 1–3 walk you through VS Code and your chosen assistant before you are expected to use it. If you are unsure which assistant or account to use, ask Big Chris before the workshop.

The starter project contains a file named CLAUDE.md. That is simply the existing filename for the workshop's project instructions. You do not have to use Claude: if your assistant does not read that file automatically, ask it to read CLAUDE.md at the start of the session.

Minimum requirements

Recommended:

  • macOS 13+ or Windows 11 (older versions usually work but are not guaranteed)
  • 8 GB RAM minimum (16 GB preferred)
  • 10 GB free disk space
  • Reliable internet connection
  • Admin access on your machine so you can install software
  • Access to your chosen AI coding assistant

Corporate laptop warning: some work machines block developer tools, AI assistants, or VS Code extensions through IT policy. Do setup at least a day before the workshop so there is time to request access or arrange another device.

What you're going to install

By the end of setup, you'll have:

Tool What it does Cost
Visual Studio Code The editor where you'll work with your project Free
An AI coding assistant for VS Code Your pair programmer inside the editor Depends on your chosen provider and plan
Antigravity IDE — alternative to the two rows above Editor with a built-in AI assistant Check your account's current access and limits
Node.js Runs the website locally so you can preview it Free

This guide does not require or recommend a particular commercial AI subscription. Confirm your assistant's access, usage limits, and costs with its provider or your organisation before the workshop.

A note on package managers (Mac users especially)

If you're already comfortable with Homebrew, Chocolatey, Scoop, or NVM, use what you prefer.

Otherwise, please use the official installers linked in this guide. Mixed package-manager installations are a common cause of “command not found” or “wrong version” problems during workshops. Standardising on the official installers makes troubleshooting much faster.

Step 1 — Install and open Visual Studio Code (5–10 minutes)

Using Antigravity? You do not need a separate VS Code installation. Continue to Step 2 and choose Route C; its editor installation is included there.

We mean Visual Studio Code, also called VS Code, with the blue ribbon-shaped icon. Visual Studio is a different application. You do not need to open PowerShell or type any commands during Steps 1–3.

Download VS Code for your operating system from https://code.visualstudio.com/download and install it:

  • Windows: use the User Installer and keep Add to PATH selected.
  • Mac: open the .dmg download and drag Visual Studio Code into Applications.

Already installed? Open it and continue below. If installation is blocked by your organisation, contact your IT team rather than changing security settings.

Find your way around VS Code

You should now see a window titled Visual Studio Code, with File, Edit, and View menus. A Welcome or getting-started tab is also normal. On Mac, these menus are in the menu bar at the very top of your screen.

This is the editor. The “Open Chat” shortcut and top “Sign In” button are not the Claude or Codex setup instructions. We will open your chosen assistant explicitly in Step 3.

You're done with this step when: this editor window is open. Leave it open and continue to Step 2.

Step 2 — Choose the assistant you will set up (1 minute)

You do not need to know how to open or sign in to an assistant yet. Step 3 shows you.

  • If you are using your approved Claude account, follow Route A: Claude Code below.
  • If you are using your approved ChatGPT/Codex account, follow Route B: Codex below.
  • If you are using Google Antigravity, follow Route C: Antigravity IDE below.

Choose one route only: A, B, or C. Use your existing approved account; do not create a separately billed API account just to get through setup.

Next: follow your chosen route in Step 3. The sign-in happens there, not here.

Step 3 — Install your assistant, open it, and get your first reply (10 minutes)

An extension adds a tool to VS Code. Installing the extension does not necessarily open its chat. We will do those as separate actions.

3.1 — Choose your assistant

Click your assistant's name below to expand its setup instructions. Leave the other sections closed. At the bottom of your section, click Continue to setup handover.

Claude/Codex screenshots show Windows; Antigravity screenshots are Google's examples. The extension names are the same on Mac; use the Mac shortcuts where given. Colours and button positions can change with updates. Match the names and publisher, not just the colour or icon.

Claude Code — expand setup instructions

Route A — Claude Code

Open the Extensions panel

Click View in VS Code's top menu, then click Extensions. Alternatively, press Ctrl + Shift + X on Windows or Cmd + Shift + X on Mac.

You should see an Extensions panel with a box labelled Search Extensions in Marketplace. The four-square icon on the far-left also opens this panel.

Your list may be empty or different. This example already has both workshop assistants installed; you only need your chosen one. Click in the search box, not the editor's top search bar.

A1 — Find and install the correct extension

Click Search Extensions in Marketplace and paste @id:anthropic.claude-code. This searches for the exact extension, avoiding similarly named tools. Click Claude Code for VS Code, published by Anthropic, in the results. Then click Install on its details page.

Check “Anthropic” before installing. If you already see Disable and Uninstall, it is installed: do not uninstall it. If asked whether you trust the publisher, check that it is Anthropic before approving. Wait until installation finishes; click Restart Extensions or Reload Window only if VS Code offers it.

A2 — Open the command picker

Click View → Command Palette…. A search box appears near the top of the editor. This searches actions you can run, not extensions or files.

Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P on Windows; Cmd + Shift + P on Mac. Leave the leading > in the box.

A3 — Open Claude's chat

Type Claude Code into that box. In the results, click Claude Code: Open in New Tab. Do not choose Open in Terminal for this walkthrough.

A tab labelled “Claude Code” should open. Later, you can repeat these two actions whenever you cannot find Claude's chat.

A4 — Choose your sign-in method

In the Claude Code tab, click Claude.ai Subscription if you are using your approved Claude subscription. Do not click the unrelated blue Sign In button in VS Code's top bar.

Anthropic Console is a separate API-billing route, not a required extra account. If your organisation uses one of the other methods, ask it for its setup instructions instead of guessing.

Complete sign-in in your browser, then return to the Claude Code tab in VS Code. You should now see a message box instead of the account-choice screen. If account access is blocked, ask Big Chris before purchasing anything.

A5 — Send your first message

Click the message box in the Claude Code tab. Type Hello! Please reply to confirm this chat is working. Do not run commands or change files. Click the send-arrow button beside the message box and wait for a reply.

Example from Anthropic's VS Code documentation, not a screenshot of your account. Its example project and message will differ. You only need a reply at this point; you do not need a project open yet.

Claude setup complete once you receive a reply. Continue to setup handover →

Codex — expand setup instructions

Route B — Codex

Open the Extensions panel

In VS Code, click View → Extensions, or press Ctrl + Shift + X on Windows / Cmd + Shift + X on Mac.

Use Search Extensions in Marketplace in this panel, not the editor's top search bar. Your installed-extension list may differ.

B1 — Find and install the correct extension

Click Search Extensions in Marketplace and paste @id:openai.chatgpt. Click Codex – OpenAI's coding agent, published by OpenAI, then click Install on its details page. The extension ID contains “chatgpt”; that is expected.

If you already see Disable and Uninstall, installation is complete. If asked whether you trust the publisher, check that it is OpenAI before approving. Wait for installation to finish and use Restart Extensions or Reload Window only if offered.

B2 — Open the command picker

Click View → Command Palette…. A search box appears near the top of VS Code.

Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P on Windows; Cmd + Shift + P on Mac. Leave the leading > in the box.

B3 — Open Codex's chat

Type Codex: Open Codex Sidebar, then click that matching result. The Codex panel should open beside the editor. It may be on the right or left depending on your layout.

Use this command again whenever you lose the panel. The ordinary VS Code “Chat” tab is a different entry point; choose the panel labelled “Codex”. Official Codex IDE instructions.

B4 — Start signing in from the Codex panel

Click Sign in with ChatGPT inside the Codex panel. Use the ChatGPT account agreed in Step 2. Do not use the unrelated VS Code sign-in button at the top of the editor or choose an API-key billing route unless your organisation specifically instructed you to.

Complete sign-in in your browser, then return to the Codex panel in VS Code. You should now see a message box. If account access is blocked, ask Big Chris before purchasing anything.

B5 — Send your first message

Click the message box in Codex. Type Hello! Please reply to confirm this chat is working. Do not run commands or change files. Click its send-arrow button and wait for a reply. You do not need to choose a special model or run a terminal command for this test.

If Codex requests a project folder before letting you chat, stop and send Big Chris that screen; the workshop project is not opened until Step 10.

Codex setup complete once you receive a reply. Continue to setup handover →

Antigravity IDE — expand setup instructions

Route C — Antigravity IDE

Complete C1–C5, then click Continue to setup handover. You do not need the Claude or Codex sections.

C1 — Install and open Antigravity IDE

Download Antigravity IDE for your computer from Google's IDE page. If you already have the Antigravity app, its Install IDE button also starts this. Open the IDE, sign in with Google, and choose your theme.

C2 — Set up the editor

On How do you want to use the Antigravity IDE Agent?, select Review-driven development, then Next.

Select the second row. Google's example has Custom configuration selected; do not copy that selection.

On Configure Your Editor, choose Normal keybindings. The Python and other language extensions shown are not needed for this workshop. The command-line launcher is optional; we will use the editor.

Leave unrelated extensions and Google Cloud plugins unselected. Finish setup to reach the editor. Setup screenshots: Google's Antigravity IDE codelab.

C3 — Find the Agent chat panel

The chat is the Agent panel on the right, not the terminal. If hidden, click the top-right layout button showing a shaded right-hand panel. On Mac, Cmd + L also toggles the agent panel.

If chat asks for a folder, click Open Folder and create/select an empty workshop-setup folder in Documents. The actual website repository comes in Step 10; do not clone it early.

C4 — Find the model selector

Click the model name and down-arrow underneath the message box to open the model list. You can leave the default selected for setup. Selecting a Claude model here keeps you in Antigravity; it does not open Claude Code.

Model names may change. The toolbar above the message box tracks changes, processes, and artifacts; it is not the model selector. Google's agent-panel documentation.

C5 — Send your first message

Click Ask anything… in the Agent panel and type:

Hello! Please reply to confirm this chat is working. Do not run commands or change files.

Press Enter to send. Wait for a reply, then keep this chat open for the handover.

Antigravity setup complete once you receive a reply. Stay in Antigravity IDE. Continue to setup handover →

3.2 — Setup handover (everyone)

All three routes rejoin here. Use the assistant you just opened—Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity.

You have now received your first reply. Stay in that same chat. Copy the whole message below, click the chat's message box, paste it, and click the send arrow:

Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigChrisCooke/workshop-template/master/WORKSHOP-SETUP-AGENT.md in full. Follow it as the controlling instructions for the rest of my workshop setup. Do not install or change anything yet. Tell me when you have read it.

Wait for the assistant to confirm that it has read the handover. The handover tells it which commands are valid, how to separate commands from expected output, and what it must not change during setup. If it cannot open the link, open that URL in your browser, copy the file's text into the same chat, and ask it to read it before continuing.

Then send:

I am on Step 4 of the workshop setup guide. Help me with one step at a time, following the setup handover. Explain each proposed change before asking my permission. Do not skip ahead, run forced dependency upgrades, or claim that a check passed without actually checking it.

You're done with this step when: your chosen assistant has replied to your first message and read the setup handover. File access and the working website will be tested after you open the actual workshop project in Steps 10–11; a chatbot saying it can do something is not that test.

Claude/Codex troubleshooting — only if a chat does not open

Open View → Extensions and search for your chosen extension ID again. Install means it is not installed yet; Enable means it is installed but disabled. Install or enable it, then retry the opening command from A3 or B3.

If the command is still missing, open View → Command Palette…, type Developer: Reload Window, and click that result. After the editor reloads, retry A3 or B3. If that does not work, send Big Chris the step number and a screenshot. At this point you should not have to use an AI or PowerShell to repair the AI setup.

Switching assistants is not the same as switching models

To move from Claude Code to Codex, open Codex: Open Codex Sidebar. To go back, open Claude Code: Open in New Tab. These are separate chats and do not automatically share your previous conversation. Give a newly chosen assistant the setup handover in Step 3.2 before asking it to continue.

A model selector changes the model within an assistant. Choosing a Claude model in a different product does not open the Claude Code extension. You can leave the model on its default for the first-message test.

Your AI assistant can now help with the rest of setup

If a command fails, an installer behaves oddly, or a permissions error appears, paste the exact error message into your assistant and ask it to explain the next safe step.

For example:

“I'm following the workshop setup guide and I'm on Step 4. When I run node --version in PowerShell, I get this error: [paste the error]. What should I do?”

“I installed Git, but git --version says ‘command not found.’ I'm on macOS. How do I fix this?”

If your assistant accepts images, you can also attach a screenshot. Include a short question such as “What does this error mean?”

Always read permission prompts before approving them. If a suggested command asks to delete files, change security settings, or requests administrator access you were not expecting, stop and ask Big Chris.

Step 4 — Install Node.js (5 minutes)

Node.js lets your computer run the website locally so you can preview it while building.

Recommended: use the official installer

  1. Go to https://nodejs.org/en/download.

  2. Make sure LTS and your operating system are selected. The workshop project requires Node 22.12 or newer; the current Node 24 LTS is recommended.

  3. Do not use the Docker instructions shown in the large command box. Scroll down to the prebuilt download buttons instead:

    • Windows: select Windows Installer (.msi).
    • Mac: select macOS Installer (.pkg).

  4. Open the downloaded installer and accept the defaults.

  5. When installation finishes, close any terminal windows that were already open. Then open a new terminal:

    • Mac: press Cmd + Space, type “Terminal,” and press Enter.
    • Windows: press the Windows key, type “PowerShell,” and press Enter.

  6. At the terminal prompt, type or paste only the command inside this box, then press Enter:

    node --version

    Do not add the word run, and do not type a version number yourself.

PowerShell should print a result similar to this on the next line:

v24.21.0

Your exact number may differ. Any Node 24 version, or a Node 22 version of at least v22.12.0, is suitable.

You're done with this step when: node --version prints Node 22.12 or newer.

Step 5 — Install Git (5 minutes)

Git tracks every change made to your project. Mac users may already have it installed.

Mac

  1. Open Terminal.
  2. Run git --version.
  3. If it prints a version number, you're done.
  4. If macOS asks to install developer tools, approve the official prompt and wait for it to finish.

Windows

  1. Go to https://git-scm.com/downloads.
  2. Select Download for Windows.
  3. Open the installer and accept the defaults.
  4. Open a new PowerShell window and run git --version.

Optional: ask your AI assistant

You may ask your assistant to check whether Git is installed and guide you through the official installation. It should explain any command and ask permission before using administrator access.

You're done with this step when: git --version prints a version number.

Step 6 — Create a GitHub account (5 minutes)

GitHub is where your project's code will live online. A free account is enough for this workshop.

  1. Go to https://github.com/signup.
  2. Sign up with an email address you check regularly.
  3. Choose a simple, professional username. It will become part of your project URLs.
  4. Verify your email address.

You're done with this step when: you can sign in to GitHub and see your username.

Step 7 — Tell Git who you are (2 minutes)

Git needs a name and email address to label the changes you save. This is a one-time setup on each machine.

Open Terminal on Mac or PowerShell on Windows and run these commands, replacing the examples with your own details:

git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
git config --global user.name "Your Name"

No output means the commands worked.

You may ask your AI assistant to run these commands, but check that it uses your correct name and email address before approving them.

You're done with this step when: both commands run without an error.

Step 8 — Create a Vercel account (5 minutes)

Vercel is where your finished website will be hosted. Sign up using your GitHub account so the two services are already linked.

  1. Go to https://vercel.com/signup.
  2. Select Continue with GitHub.
  3. Review and approve the requested GitHub access.
  4. Choose a simple username or Hobby team name.
  5. Skip any “import a project” prompts for now.

You're done with this step when: you can sign in to Vercel and see your dashboard.

Step 9 — Create your project from the workshop template (5 minutes)

Instead of setting up a website from scratch, you'll begin with a ready-made starter project. It includes the website tools, a brand.md brief, and a CLAUDE.md project-instructions file that any suitable AI assistant can read when asked.

  1. Go to https://github.com/BigChrisCooke/workshop-template.
  2. Select the green Use this template button.
  3. Select Create a new repository.
  4. Give it a name, such as my-first-site.
  5. Select Public so Vercel can deploy it during the workshop.
  6. Select Create repository.
  7. GitHub will create your copy. Note its URL, which will look like github.com/your-username/my-first-site.

You're done with this step when: you can see your new repository at its own GitHub URL.

Step 10 — Clone the project and open it in VS Code (5 minutes)

“Cloning” means downloading your GitHub repository to your computer so you can work on it locally.

Recommended: clone from VS Code

  1. Copy the URL of the repository you created in Step 9.
  2. Open VS Code.
  3. Press Ctrl + Shift + P on Windows or Cmd + Shift + P on Mac.
  4. Type Git: Clone and select it.
  5. Paste your repository URL and press Enter.
  6. Choose a sensible location, such as a projects folder inside Documents.
  7. When cloning finishes, select Open.
  8. If VS Code asks whether you trust the authors of the files, confirm only after checking that the folder is your copy of BigChrisCooke/workshop-template.

Optional: ask your AI assistant

If your assistant can clone repositories from inside VS Code, you may ask:

Please clone my GitHub repository at https://github.com/your-username/my-first-site into a projects folder inside my Documents folder, then help me open it in VS Code. Explain the command before running it.

You should now see CLAUDE.md, brand.md, and package.json in the file explorer on the left.

You're done with this step when: VS Code shows your cloned project folder and those files are visible.

Step 11 — Install and test the actual workshop project (10–15 minutes)

This is the step that proves the full toolchain works together. Run everything from the VS Code terminal while the cloned project folder is open.

Test 1 — Open the terminal in VS Code

Select Terminal → New Terminal in VS Code.

Test 2 — Check versions

Run:

node --version
git --version

Node must be 22.12 or newer. Each command should print a version number.

Test 3 — Install the project's dependencies

Run:

npm ci

This uses the template's lockfile so everyone installs the same dependency versions. It may take a few minutes. The maintained template should report 0 vulnerabilities.

Do not run npm audit fix or npm audit fix --force, even if npm suggests it. If npm reports any high or critical vulnerabilities, stop and send Big Chris a screenshot; the template needs a maintainer update. Continue only when npm ci finishes without an npm ERR! failure and without high or critical audit findings.

Test 4 — Download the matching Playwright browser

Run this after npm ci and from the project folder:

npx playwright install chromium

Playwright browser versions are tied to the Playwright version in the project. Running the command here avoids downloading a browser that does not match the workshop template. The download is several hundred megabytes and may take longer on a corporate network.

Test 5 — Build the site

Run:

npm run build

You are looking for a successful build with no error. If it fails, copy the complete error into your AI assistant and say you are on Step 11, Test 5.

Test 6 — Open the local preview

Run:

npm run dev

The command keeps running while the preview server is open; that is expected. Open the localhost address shown in the terminal, normally http://localhost:4321/. Confirm that a page loads, then return to the terminal and press Ctrl + C to stop the server.

Test 7 — Check your AI assistant's project access

Open your assistant inside VS Code and send:

Please read CLAUDE.md in this project and tell me one workshop rule it contains. Do not edit any files yet.

If the assistant cannot find the file, confirm that the cloned project folder—not its parent folder—is open in VS Code. Some assistants do not load CLAUDE.md automatically, which is fine; they only need to read it when asked.

You're fully ready when:

  • Node is version 22.12 or newer.
  • Git prints a version.
  • npm ci finishes successfully.
  • Playwright Chromium downloads successfully.
  • npm run build finishes successfully.
  • The site opens at the localhost address shown in the terminal.
  • Your AI assistant reports one specific rule from CLAUDE.md.

Step 12 — Prepare your personalisation brief (5 minutes)

Before Session 1, decide what your version of the site will be about. The structure stays the same; you will change the content to make it yours.

Write down three things:

  1. What the site is about, in one sentence
    Example: “A fictional Jira time-tracking app called TimeWise.”
  2. Your main headline
    Example: “Track every hour in Jira, automatically.”
  3. Your brand colour
    Example: “deep teal,” “forest green,” or “burnt orange.”

Stuck for ideas? Choose your own job or business, a hobby, or a fictional Atlassian Marketplace app.

You're done with this step when: those three decisions are written somewhere you can find during Session 1.

Quick troubleshooting

First port of call: paste the exact error into your AI coding assistant and say which step you are following. Read any proposed command before approving it.

“Command not found” appears for node --version or git --version

  • Close and reopen the terminal. Newly installed programs appear only in new terminal sessions.
  • On Windows, restart the computer if a new terminal still cannot find the command.

PowerShell says run is not recognised

  • Node is probably installed correctly; the instruction label was entered as part of the command.
  • At the PS C:\...> prompt, enter exactly node --version.
  • Do not enter run node, and do not add the version you expect to see. The version is PowerShell's output, not part of the command.

The Node download page is showing Docker commands

  • You do not need Docker for this workshop.
  • Confirm that LTS and your operating system are selected, then scroll down and choose the prebuilt Windows Installer (.msi) or macOS Installer (.pkg).

My AI assistant is unavailable or says I've reached a usage limit

  • Check your provider's account status and usage-limit information.
  • Avoid pasting entire large files when only one error or section is relevant.
  • Ask Big Chris about the workshop fallback; do not purchase an upgrade under time pressure.

My AI assistant cannot access the project

  • Confirm the cloned project folder is open in VS Code.
  • Check that the assistant has permission to read the workspace.
  • Follow the provider's official instructions for connecting it to VS Code.

My assistant cannot see CLAUDE.md

  • Ask it explicitly to read CLAUDE.md from the project root.
  • Confirm the file is visible in VS Code's file explorer.
  • If the file is missing, clone the workshop template again or ask Big Chris for help.

I can't find the workshop template

  • Go to https://github.com/BigChrisCooke/workshop-template.
  • Sign in to GitHub if the Use this template button is missing.

Git asks me for credentials when I push

  • Do not enter your normal GitHub password into an unfamiliar prompt.
  • Follow GitHub's current official authentication instructions or ask Big Chris for help.

A terminal command looks frozen

  • See “Normal developer-tool behaviour” below.

Normal developer-tool behaviour

Some terminal commands keep running — that can be correct

When you start a local web server with:

npm run dev

the terminal prints startup messages and then waits. It has not crashed; it is keeping the preview server running.

To stop it, select that terminal and press Ctrl + C on Windows or Mac.

AI assistants ask for permission

An assistant may ask before reading files, editing files, or running a terminal command. This is a safety feature.

Read the proposed action before approving it. Stop and ask for help if it wants to delete files, change security settings, expose credentials, or use administrator access unexpectedly.

AI services can have usage limits

Limits vary by provider and account plan. If your assistant becomes unavailable during the workshop, save your work and tell Big Chris. A workshop fallback is better than purchasing an unplanned upgrade.

What you'll have at the end of the workshop

By the end, you'll have:

  • A live website on the internet, such as yourname.vercel.app.
  • A GitHub repository containing your code.
  • Confidence building and iterating with an AI assistant.
  • An understanding of how project instructions guide an AI assistant.
  • A reusable website-building toolchain.

Glossary

Term What it means
Astro A web framework for building fast static websites.
Tailwind A CSS framework used to style the workshop site.
Vercel A hosting service where the finished site will run.
Repo Short for repository: a project folder tracked by Git and stored on GitHub.
Commit A saved snapshot of a project's state.
Push Sending local commits to GitHub. This can trigger a Vercel deployment.
Pull request (PR) A way to propose and review changes. You will not need it for a solo workshop project.
Branch A separate line of work in a repository. The workshop will mostly use main.
Terminal A text interface for running commands: PowerShell on Windows, Terminal on Mac, or VS Code's built-in terminal.
npm Node Package Manager, used to install and run project tools.
localhost Your own computer. A local preview might use an address such as http://localhost:4321.
CLAUDE.md The existing project-instructions filename in the workshop template. Any suitable AI assistant can read it when asked, even if it does not load it automatically.
Vibe coding Building software by directing an AI assistant in plain language instead of writing every line by hand.
Playwright A tool that takes browser screenshots so you can compare a rebuild with its reference site.

Pre-workshop checklist

  • VS Code is installed and opens cleanly.
  • I can sign in to an AI coding assistant inside VS Code.
  • My assistant can work with the project folder open in VS Code.
  • node --version prints Node 22.12 or newer.
  • git --version prints a version.
  • I can sign in to GitHub.
  • Git has my name and email.
  • I can sign in to Vercel through GitHub.
  • I created a repository from https://github.com/BigChrisCooke/workshop-template.
  • I cloned the repository and can see CLAUDE.md, brand.md, and package.json in VS Code.
  • npm ci and npm run build both finish without an error.
  • Playwright Chromium downloaded successfully with npx playwright install chromium from the project folder.
  • The project opens at the localhost address shown by npm run dev.
  • My AI assistant read CLAUDE.md and reported one specific workshop rule.
  • I wrote down my site topic, headline, and brand colour.

If every box is ticked, you're ready. See you in Session 1!
